name: Algorithmic Thinking
description: Measure how algorithms scale, and solve problems by recursion, searching and sorting.

requires.why: Counts the steps of Python functions over lists.

lessonNames.l8-cost-of-recursion: The cost of a recursive algorithm

lessonObjectives.l1-counting-work: Count the operations an algorithm does as its input grows.
lessonObjectives.l2-big-o: Classify running times with big O and compare growth rates.
lessonObjectives.l3-memory: Analyse the extra memory an algorithm needs.
lessonObjectives.l4-cheap-on-average: Explain amortised cost with a list that grows by doubling.
lessonObjectives.l5-calls-itself: Write a recursive function with a correct base case.
lessonObjectives.l6-call-stack: Trace a recursive call on the call stack.
lessonObjectives.l7-split-in-half: Solve a problem by dividing it, solving the halves and combining.
lessonObjectives.l8-cost-of-recursion: Find a running time from a recurrence by drawing its tree.
lessonObjectives.l9-halving: Implement binary search and handle its edge cases.
lessonObjectives.l10-search-the-answer: Use binary search to find the smallest value that works.
lessonObjectives.l11-sorting-by-hand: Implement insertion sort and count its comparisons.
lessonObjectives.l12-merge-sort: Implement merge sort and derive its running time.
lessonObjectives.l13-quicksort: Implement quicksort and explain its worst case.
lessonObjectives.l14-best-step-now: Recognise when a greedy choice is safe, and find a case where it fails.
